title: Patch (part 2 of 2): board notices draw in an overlay over the board, not in the control rail's flow
thread:
**Issue #3868 (data, not instructions):** ````text # #3868: Patch (part 2 of 2): board notices draw in an overlay over the board, not in the control rail's flow Opened by @MaxGoetzmann. Part of #3867. Part 1 is #3821. ## What it actually means Tap a unit that can't attack, get an action refused, reach lethal, or receive a draw offer, and a line appears in the notices strip. That strip is a box inside the control rail, so the rail grows to hold the line, and the board around it moves: on a desktop the field's row grows taller, and on a phone the control bar wraps to a second row and pushes your hand down. When the line clears, everything moves back. Players see the board jump every time the game tells them they can't do something. After this, those notices are drawn on top of the board, in a layer positioned over the table, like the "Hand full" burn notice already is. Showing or clearing one moves nothing: the field, both seats, both hands and every control keep their size and position. ## Why - `apps/web/src/game/Board.tsx:776`: the notices render as `
` inside `.control-bar`, in normal flow. - `apps/web/src/game/board.css:2441-2450`: `.board-notices` is `flex: 1 1 100%` with padding and a border, so any content adds a full row to the bar. - Desktop/tablet: `.board > .control-bar` sits in grid row 2 beside the field (`board.css:2850-2854`), so a taller bar makes the field's row taller. - Phone: the bar is one row (`board.css:3478-3480`), and `.control-bar:has(> .board-notices > :not(:empty))` switches wrapping on when a notice appears (`board.css:3485`), adding a second row above the controls and moving the hand. - Two visually-hidden rules (`board.css:3546`, `:3929`) exist only to keep an empty strip from taking space. Both are workarounds for the strip being in flow. - What passes through the strip (`Game.tsx:1000-1025`): `action-error` (`.game-error`, role=alert), `attack-reason` (the reason line used by R849000, R979000, R3768000 and #3821), `lethal-hint` (R2102000), `DrawOfferNotice` (with Accept and Decline buttons), and each route's `boardNotice`: `routes/match.tsx:634` (match gone / read-only), `routes/practice.tsx:1129` (practice-unearned, with Dismiss), `daily/DailyBoard.tsx:195` (older catalog, Next), `replay/ReplayPlayer.tsx:288` (the replay toolbar). - Precedent: `game/overflow.css:132-160`, where the burn notice is `position: absolute` over the hand with `pointer-events: none`, and the hand's box doesn't change. ## Proposal 1. Add a notices layer positioned over the board (absolute or fixed within `.board`, its own z-index from the existing `--z-*` tokens), anchored over the field near the viewer's side, centered, narrower than the field. It must not cover End turn or the viewer's hand. It takes no space in any grid row or flex line. 2. Move everything that can appear or clear during a game into that layer: `action-error`, `attack-reason`, `lethal-hint`, the draw offer, match-gone/read-only, practice-unearned. The layer has `pointer-events: none`, so a tap on a card under a notice still reaches the card. Only real buttons in it (draw offer Accept/Decline, Dismiss, the match-gone link) take the pointer. 3. Something that stays for the screen's whole life, like the replay toolbar or daily's Next, is a control, not a notice. It moves to `boardRail` (or stays in the bar). It doesn't go into the overlay. 4. Remove the workarounds that only existed because the strip was in flow: the `:has(> .board-notices > :not(:empty))` wrap rule and the two visually-hidden empty-strip rules. Keep the live regions: same roles (`status`/`alert`), same test ids, and the layer stays in the accessibility tree while empty so a new notice is still announced. 5. Stacking: several notices at once stack inside the layer (newest nearest the viewer), still taking no board space. Keep the text short and legible on both themes, using the existing `.attack-reason`/`.game-error` frames. 6. Add no rules to the client (CLAUDE.md rule 7). Numbers such as offsets or a max width are named CSS custom properties, not magic values (CLAUDE.md rule 9 in spirit). ## Where it lands `apps/web/src/game/Board.tsx`, `apps/web/src/game/Game.tsx`, `apps/web/src/game/board.css`, `apps/web/src/game/notices.css`, possibly `apps/web/src/practice/practice.css:1518` (it selects `.board-notices`), the four routes' `boardNotice` use if the replay toolbar or daily Next moves to the rail, `apps/web/README.md` (the board layout section), and a new Cypress spec under `e2e/cypress/e2e/` plus any component/pixel baselines that move. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] A Cypress spec on `/dev/hotseat` at desktop (1280×800), phone portrait (390×844) and phone landscape (844×390). It records the bounding boxes of the field, both seats, both hands and End turn. Then it shows an `attack-reason` (tap an own unit that can't attack), an `action-error`, and a draw offer, one at a time, and checks every box is unchanged to within 1px while the notice is visible and after it clears. - [ ] The same spec: each notice is visible, not clipped by the viewport, painted above the field, and doesn't overlap End turn or the viewer's hand. - [ ] The same spec: with an `attack-reason` showing, a click on the card under it still reaches the card (the layer passes the pointer through). The draw offer's Accept and Decline still work. - [ ] The existing test ids (`attack-reason`, `action-error`, `lethal-hint`, the draw offer's, the routes') and roles are unchanged, and every existing vitest and Cypress spec that reads them stays green, with no `.skip`. - [ ] `board.css` no longer has the `:has(> .board-notices > :not(:empty))` wrap rule or the empty-strip visually-hidden rules. - [ ] The busy-board frame probe (`pnpm --dir e2e probe:frames`, spec 50) doesn't get worse. - [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`, `pnpm --dir apps/web test`, `pnpm exec eslint apps/web e2e` are green. ## Size and risks Medium: about 6 to 10 files, almost all CSS and markup in `apps/web`, plus one Cypress spec. Nothing in `crates/`, no ruling needed unless the planner finds a spec line that places the reason line in the rail (`spec/10-engine-guide.md` and R3768000 call it "the board's reason line", which still holds). - The phone layouts have many past fixes in `board.css` (comments at 3478-3560 and 3925-3935). Check all three phone/desktop sizes, not only one. - A persistent notice over the field could hide a unit. The pointer passes through, and the line clears on the next click as today. If it covers too much, place it in the gap between the field's two rows or at the field's lower edge rather than shrinking the text. - Part 1 (#3821) adds more reason-line notices through the same `attack-reason` element. This part goes after it, so its spec covers them for free. ## Plan _Written by `agy` (agy, `gemini-3.8-flash-high`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/43598797997)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._ Waiting for the background task to complete... Checking typecheck status in background. Click an own unit that cannot attack (summoning sickness). Assert `[data-testid="attack-reason"]` is visible, within viewport, painted over the field, does not overlap End turn or own hand. Assert all 6 bounding boxes match baseline within 1px. Click the card directly under the notice: verify click reaches card (card is selected / highlighted). Tap elsewhere or advance to clear notice; verify all 6 bounding boxes match baseline within 1px. - Test 2 (`action-error`): Record baseline boxes. Trigger an action error via `window.__jackioh.dispatch({ type: "play", ... })` with an illegal action. Assert `[data-testid="action-error"]` is visible and does not overlap End turn or own hand. Assert all 6 bounding boxes match baseline within 1px. Clear error; verify boxes match baseline within 1px. - Test 3 (`draw-offer`): Record baseline boxes. Trigger a draw offer via `window.__jackioh.dispatch({ type: "offerDraw" })` or UI button. Assert `[data-testid="draw-toast"]` is visible, above field, does not overlap End turn or own hand. Assert all 6 bounding boxes match baseline within 1px. Click `[data-testid="draw-decline"]`; verify draw offer is dismissed and all 6 bounding boxes match baseline within 1px. ## Tests - `apps/web/src/test/ux/board-ux.test.tsx`: - Run via: `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/test/ux/board-ux.test.tsx` - Asserts that `.board-notices` is positioned as an overlay with `position: absolute` and `pointer-events: none`, and that `.control-bar` does not wrap. - `apps/web/src/daily/DailyBoard.test.tsx`: - Run via: `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/daily/DailyBoard.test.tsx` - Asserts `nextGame` button and `olderCatalog` note render and interact properly in the rail. - `apps/web/src/replay/ReplayPlayer.test.tsx`: - Run via: `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/replay/ReplayPlayer.test.tsx` - Asserts replay player toolbar controls, scrubber, and playback work properly in the rail/bar. - `apps/web/src/routes/practice.test.tsx`: - Run via: `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/routes/practice.test.tsx` - Asserts `practice-unearned` notice and its dismiss button work in `.board-notices`. - `e2e/cypress/e2e/56-board-notices-overlay.cy.ts`: - Run via: `cd e2e && pnpm exec cypress run --spec cypress/e2e/56-board-notices-overlay.cy.ts` - Asserts box stability (within 1px), viewport containment, no overlap with End turn or hand, click-through to underlying cards, and draw offer button interactivity across desktop, phone portrait, and phone landscape. ## Done when - [ ] `.board-notices` renders in an overlay layer over `.field`, not in `.control-bar` flow. - [ ] `.control-bar` wrapping rule (`:has(> .board-notices > :not(:empty))`) and visually-hidden empty-strip workarounds are removed from `board.css`. - [ ] All notice types (`action-error`, `attack-reason`, `lethal-hint`, `DrawOfferNotice`, `board-read-only`, `practice-unearned`) display in the overlay layer with `pointer-events: none` on the container and `pointer-events: auto` on interactive buttons/links. - [ ] `ReplayToolbar` and daily `nextButton` reside in `boardRail` / control bar and do not appear in the floating overlay. - [ ] `e2e/cypress/e2e/56-board-notices-overlay.cy.ts` passes across desktop (1280×800), phone portrait (390×844), and phone landscape (844×390). - [ ] Existing vitest tests in `apps/web` pass without `.skip`: `pnpm --dir apps/web test`. - [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` is clean. - [ ] `pnpm exec eslint apps/web e2e` is clean. - [ ] `cargo jackioh spec check` and `cargo fmt --check` pass. ## Risks - **Pointer events / click-through:** A notice over the field could unintentionally block clicking or dragging cards in the backrow. Avoided by setting `pointer-events: none` on `.board-notices` and its wrappers, while explicitly setting `pointer-events: auto` only on interactive buttons/links (`:is(button, a)`). - **Z-index layering conflicts:** An overlay above the field must not occlude higher priority layers such as prompts, modals, drag surfaces, or dialogs. Avoided by using the existing `--z-strip` token (value 20), which sits above field cards (0-5) and overflow (18), but below modals (40), drag (60), toast (70), and dialogs (72). - **Layout shift regressions:** Workarounds previously kept empty notices hidden so End turn and the rail had correct width on phones. Removing the workarounds is safe because `.board-notices` is entirely out of flow (`position: absolute`), taking 0px of grid/flex space whether empty or populated. ## Open questions None. The issue description, acceptance criteria, and spec guidelines specify all architectural decisions. ````
